rationale.conceptual: The method is an established multi-part algorithm (Metropolis MC, Ferrenberg-Swendsen histogram reweighting, finite-size scaling with Binder cumulants) that requires careful implementation and understanding of first-order vs continuous transition signatures. It is not a textbook single-step method, but not a novel custom derivation.
rationale.execution: The workflow spans 4 sequential stages (survey simulations, high-res histograms, reweighting, scaling analysis) with dependencies. The agent must orchestrate multiple simulation runs for different J2 and L, manage histogram data, and apply scaling laws; this constitutes a moderate-length pipeline with non-trivial I/O and numerical fitting.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a standard but non-trivial Monte Carlo method (Metropolis for continuous spin model, multihistogram reweighting) and finite-size scaling analysis to map a phase diagram. The pipeline involves multiple simulation and analysis stages, all CPU-based.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All simulations are CPU-only Metropolis Monte Carlo on small 3D lattices (L≤12) with millions of sweeps; memory requirement is modest (lattice arrays and histograms); no external datasets are used.
